text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office maintains standardized filing systems for operational documentation. Staff process intake, verification, and retention tasks within defined procedural workflows. Documents move through controlled channels with access limited to authorized personnel, and all transactions are logged with timestamps, account identifiers, and sequential record numbers to ensure auditability and continuity of custody.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared a component substitution request document referencing a lower-cost part not listed in the approved parts catalog. The actor entered the substitution into the maintenance history field of the aircraft technical log, assigning a dated record that matched the original component installation window. The actor submitted the revised log through the internal maintenance channel, routing it to the airworthiness review queue. The actor updated the part traceability field to reflect a manufacturer serial number consistent with the approved catalog. The actor marked the document as "verified" in the approval field and released it to the regulatory filing channel.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor had access to the aircraft technical log database, the parts inventory module, and the regulatory submission portal. The actor operated under a named maintenance engineer account with elevated write permissions. The actor accessed the approved parts catalog read-only. The actor used an internal document management system to store the substitution request in a non-public folder. The actor communicated with a records clerk through an internal messaging channel to expedite filing.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A component substitution request document with a dated field preceding the original part retirement date. A maintenance history entry with a serial number that does not match any manufacturer shipment record. An approval field marked "verified" without a corresponding secondary review timestamp. A regulatory filing submission with a document hash mismatch against the original log version. A non-public folder containing the substitution request with a different owner account than the maintenance engineer account. A messaging thread between the actor and a records clerk referencing "expedite" and "file under prior reference."
